name: application-board-swimlane
title: Board Swimlane
description: A board layout that groups cards into horizontal lanes (e.g. by team) spanning shared status columns, with a labeled lane header per row.
useWhen: A Kanban-style board needs a second grouping dimension (team, epic, priority) that spans across the same status columns.
Users need to compare progress across groups at each status without switching board views.
avoidWhen: There's only one grouping and no need to compare across teams/categories — a single-lane board of status columns is simpler.
The lanes would each need vastly different column sets — swimlanes assume shared columns across every lane; use separate boards instead if that assumption breaks.
responsiveBehavior: The grid uses a fixed-width lane-label column plus equal-width status columns; on narrow viewports, make the whole board horizontally scrollable rather than shrinking columns below a legible width.
accessibility: Each lane's label pairs a color dot with a text name, not color alone, so lanes are distinguishable without relying on color perception.
Completed cards use both a strikethrough and (in a real implementation) an aria-label or visually hidden text stating their status, not strikethrough styling alone.
Column headers stay visible and associated with their cards via consistent grid position across every lane.

variants.title: Team lanes
variants.description: A three-column (To Do / In Progress / Done) board with two team swimlanes (Design, Engineering), each with a colored lane label and cards including a strikethrough-styled completed state.
accessibility: Each lane pairs a color dot with a text team name.

variants.title: Team lanes (Dark)
variants.description: Board swimlane adapted for dark surfaces, including card borders and completed-card muting.
accessibility: Column headers, lane labels, and card text all meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark board background.
